chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhassin ibn Ahmad, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Hadeed ibn Hakim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The lowest degree of ingratitude (to parents) is the saying 'Uff' (a sigh of impatience), and if Allah had known of anything less than it, He would have forbidden it.

key_terms.أُفٍّ: A sigh of impatience or mild annoyance

ai.seo_question: What is the lowest form of disrespect towards parents in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies uttering 'Uff'—a sigh of mild impatience—as the baseline of ingratitude (uqoq), noting that if it were less significant, God would not have prohibited it. This highlights the meticulous nature of Shia ethical training, where even subtle non-verbal cues of annoyance are scrutinized to preserve the sanctity of parental respect. The hadith underscores that the prohibition is rooted in divine wisdom, elevating minor gestures to the status of moral obligations.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhassin Bin Ahmad, from Aban Bin usman, from Hadeed Bin Hakeym, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdulllah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The lowest of the disloyalty is (the saying of) ‘Ugh’, and had Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Known of anything less than it, He<sup>azwj</sup> would have Forbidden from it’.
en.sarwar: 9. Abu Ali al-Ash’ari has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhsin ibn Ahmad from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from Hadid ibn Hakim from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘
The minimum form of causing suffering and disappointment to parents is the expression, ‘Uff. Had Allah known anything less disappointing than ‘Uff, He would have prohibited it.’”
